To turn your unstructured chat dumps into an actionable project graph, you need a pipeline that moves from raw exports to topic segmentation, hyperedge linking, and development scoring.

1. Data Ingestion & Canonical Storage

  • Extraction: Rather than running an unauthenticated browser scraper that risks session drops, export your complete archive directly via Google Takeout (JSON/HTML export under Gemini/Apps data), or use your scraper to write raw records directly into a canonical format.
  • Storage Engine (SQLite): Store raw messages in an append-only relational database to serve as the single source of truth:
    • threads (thread_id, created_at, updated_at, title)
    • messages (message_id, thread_id, role, timestamp, content_raw, tokens_approx)

2. Topic Segmentation & Branch Detection (Head States)

Because long-running chats drift across distinct subjects (e.g., hardware debugging morphing into software architecture or physical builds), you need to segment threads into semantic blocks:

  • Boundary Detection: Run sliding-window semantic cosine similarity (or a lightweight local LLM pass) across sequential turns to detect abrupt topic shifts.
  • Branch/Block Unit:
    • thread_blocks (block_id, thread_id, start_message_id, end_message_id, dominant_topic, summary)
    • This isolates multi-topic chats into discrete chronological segments rather than treating an entire months-long conversation as a single entity.

3. Hypergraph Metadata & Entity Extraction

Map each block into your decentralized graph structure using YAML frontmatter metadata or relational edges:

  • Hyperedges & N-ary Relations: Connect blocks not just by parent-child threads, but across independent threads sharing domains (e.g., linking an OpenSCAD script discussion to a physical build thread and an embedded firmware branch).
  • Tagging Schema:
    • Domain: Software / Hardware / Physical Build / Music / Research
    • Artifacts Generated: Code snippets, schematics, CAD models, formulas, or instructional steps.
    • Status / Exit State: Blocked, Prototype Complete, Architecture Draft, Solved, Abandoned.

4. Quantifying Development & Investment Score

To gauge how much time and energy went into each initiative, calculate a composite Maturity & Investment Metric ($S_{\text{dev}}$) for every extracted project/cluster:

$$S_{\text{dev}} = w_1 (\text{Total Turns}) + w_2 (\text{Code/Artifact Density}) + w_3 (\text{Duration Days}) + w_4 (\text{Linkage Density})$$

  • High Effort / Dormant Filter: Query for projects with high $S_{\text{dev}}$ and high token volume, but with a large days_since_last_interaction (high staleness). These represent substantial investments that stalled right at the finish line.
